00001| """Immutable, content-addressed state nodes for the context-cache experiment.
00002| 
00003| A :class:`StateNode` is the unit of context state.  Its ``node_id`` is the
00004| sha256 of its canonical bytes, so identity *is* content: two nodes with the
00005| same text and the same parent are the same node, and any change to the text
00006| yields a different address.  There is deliberately no ``edit()`` method -- the
00007| only way to change state is to create a new node on a new chain.
00008| 
00009| The private ``_parent`` field keeps the object graph (so :meth:`chain` can walk
00010| to the root without a global registry) and is excluded from equality, repr and
00011| hashing: two nodes are equal iff their content addresses are equal.
00012| """
00013| 
00014| from __future__ import annotations
00015| 
00016| import hashlib
00017| import json
00018| from dataclasses import dataclass, field
00019| from typing import Any, Mapping
00020| 
00021| KINDS: frozenset[str] = frozenset({"invariant", "pointer", "delta", "summary", "fork"})
00022| 
00023| 
00024| def canonical_bytes(obj: Any) -> bytes:
00025|     """Stable JSON bytes for hashing: sorted keys, no whitespace, UTF-8."""
00026| 
00027|     return json.dumps(
00028|         obj,
00029|         sort_keys=True,
00030|         separators=(",", ":"),
00031|         ensure_ascii=False,
00032|         default=str,
00033|     ).encode("utf-8")
00034| 
00035| 
00036| def digest(obj: Any) -> str:
00037|     """sha256 hex of :func:`canonical_bytes`."""
00038| 
00039|     return hashlib.sha256(canonical_bytes(obj)).hexdigest()
00040| 
00041| 
00042| @dataclass(frozen=True)
00043| class StateNode:
00044|     """One immutable state node.  ``node_id`` is a content address."""
00045| 
00046|     node_id: str
00047|     parent_id: str | None
00048|     kind: str
00049|     text: str
00050|     meta: Mapping[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict, compare=False)
00051|     # Object-graph back-pointer used by chain(); not part of identity.
00052|     _parent: "StateNode | None" = field(default=None, compare=False, repr=False)
00053| 
00054|     # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
00055|     # Construction
00056|     # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
00057|     @classmethod
00058|     def create(
00059|         cls,
00060|         text: str,
00061|         kind: str,
00062|         parent: "StateNode | None" = None,
00063|         **meta: Any,
00064|     ) -> "StateNode":
00065|         """Create a node whose id is the hash of (kind, text, parent, meta)."""
00066| 
00067|         if not isinstance(text, str):
00068|             raise TypeError("text must be a str")
00069|         if kind not in KINDS:
00070|             raise ValueError(f"unknown node kind {kind!r}; expected one of {sorted(KINDS)}")
00071|         parent_id = parent.node_id if parent is not None else None
00072|         meta_dict = dict(meta)
00073|         node_id = digest(
00074|             {
00075|                 "kind": kind,
00076|                 "text": text,
00077|                 "parent": parent_id,
00078|                 "meta": meta_dict,
00079|             }
00080|         )
00081|         return cls(
00082|             node_id=node_id,
00083|             parent_id=parent_id,
00084|             kind=kind,
00085|             text=text,
00086|             meta=meta_dict,
00087|             _parent=parent,
00088|         )
00089| 
00090|     # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
00091|     # Chain helpers
00092|     # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
00093|     def chain(self) -> list["StateNode"]:
00094|         """Return ``root..self`` order."""
00095| 
00096|         out: list[StateNode] = []
00097|         node: StateNode | None = self
00098|         seen: set[str] = set()
00099|         while node is not None:
00100|             if node.node_id in seen:  # pragma: no cover - defensive against cycles
00101|                 raise ValueError(f"cycle in node chain at {node.node_id}")
00102|             seen.add(node.node_id)
00103|             out.append(node)
00104|             if node._parent is None and node.parent_id is not None:
00105|                 raise ValueError(
00106|                     f"node {node.node_id} names parent {node.parent_id} but its "
00107|                     "parent object is not attached; rebuild the chain with create()"
00108|                 )
00109|             node = node._parent
00110|         out.reverse()
00111|         return out
00112| 
00113|     @property
00114|     def chain_hash(self) -> str:
00115|         """sha256 over ``[(node_id, kind), ...]`` in root..self order."""
00116| 
00117|         return digest([[n.node_id, n.kind] for n in self.chain()])
00118| 
00119|     # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
00120|     # Serialisation
00121|     # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
00122|     def to_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
00123|         return {
00124|             "node_id": self.node_id,
00125|             "parent_id": self.parent_id,
00126|             "kind": self.kind,
00127|             "text": self.text,
00128|             "meta": dict(self.meta),
00129|         }
00130| 
00131|     @classmethod
00132|     def from_dict(cls, data: Mapping[str, Any]) -> "StateNode":
00133|         """Rehydrate a node without its parent linkage (``_parent`` is None)."""
00134| 
00135|         return cls(
00136|             node_id=str(data["node_id"]),
00137|             parent_id=data.get("parent_id"),
00138|             kind=str(data["kind"]),
00139|             text=str(data["text"]),
00140|             meta=dict(data.get("meta") or {}),
00141|         )
00142| 
00143|     def __str__(self) -> str:  # pragma: no cover - cosmetic
00144|         return f"StateNode({self.kind}, {self.node_id[:12]}, {len(self.text)} chars)"

00145| """Render policies: how a state chain becomes OpenAI ``messages``.
00146| 
00147| Two rules keep the comparison honest, and both are asserted in
00148| ``tests/test_context_render.py``:
00149| 
00150| 1. **A message, once emitted, is never rewritten by a later turn.**  Every
00151|    history node renders from its own ``node.text``, verbatim, in chain order.
00152|    Appending turn N+1 therefore appends one message and leaves the first N
00153|    history messages byte-identical: turn N's message list is a prefix of turn
00154|    N+1's, and the newline-joined concatenation of message contents is likewise
00155|    a prefix.  (The canonical-JSON blob is not literally a byte prefix, because
00156|    serialising an array writes its closing ``]`` only at the end; the tests
00157|    state the exact JSON relation they assert.)
00158| 2. **Equal information.**  ``POINTER`` and ``NAIVE_APPEND`` send the same chain
00159|    content for the same chain -- every body, in order, byte for byte.
00160|    :func:`equal_information` asserts it.  What distinguishes the pointer arm is
00161|    how the chain was *built* -- content-addressed nodes, fork-instead-of-edit,
00162|    one node shared across several chains -- not the omission of earlier turn
00163|    bodies.  Comparing the arms therefore measures caching, not a smaller
00164|    prompt.
00165| 
00166| ``POINTER``
00167|     Salted invariant preamble (salt first), then every body in chain order,
00168|     verbatim.  Appending a turn appends one message; nothing earlier changes.
00169| 
00170| ``NAIVE_APPEND``
00171|     The same salted preamble and the same bodies in the same order, built by
00172|     plain append: for the same chain it is byte-identical to ``POINTER``.  The
00173|     salt is per cell, not per arm -- without it one cell could be served
00174|     another cell's radix-cache prefix, which would corrupt both arms.
00175| 
00176| ``NAIVE_MUTABLE``
00177|     Volatile values are interpolated *into the preamble message*, so changing
00178|     one value rewrites message 0 on every turn and invalidates the prefix.
00179|     This is the sensitivity bound under test -- not a bug to "fix", and
00180|     deliberately not equal-information with the other two.
00181| 
00182| ``POINTER_FORK``
00183|     ``POINTER`` over a chain whose root is a fork, with the fork labelled in
00184|     the invariant preamble (root address): the label is how a
00185|     compaction-caused prefix break is identified.  If the root is not a fork
00186|     the label is omitted and the rendering equals ``POINTER``.  The fork node's
00187|     own body also starts with the content-addressed provenance marker that
00188|     :func:`resextract.context.budget.compact` writes (replaced-head pointer +
00189|     forked-from chain hash), so the distinction survives any renderer -- a
00190|     summary node carries no marker in either rendering.
00191| 
00192| Volatile values are never re-attached to an already-emitted body.  A body is
00193| its node's text; the only policy that adds the current volatile block to the
00194| prompt is ``NAIVE_MUTABLE``, which puts it in the invariant header.  The two
00195| append-only policies send no volatile block at all rather than rewrite history
00196| to carry it -- an honest baseline may carry less volatile metadata, but it may
00197| not manufacture a cache miss by rewriting an emitted message.
00198| 
00199| ``APPEND_NOTE`` chains need no renderer of their own, and no new branch here:
00200| the note is a ``summary`` node appended at the tail, and both node selectors --
00201| :func:`_body_nodes` for the append-only policies and :func:`_history` for
00202| ``NAIVE_MUTABLE`` -- already include every non-invariant ``summary`` node.  So
00203| the note's own ``[note] ...`` marker reaches the transcript verbatim under all
00204| four policies, and the distinction from ``SUMMARISE_IN_PLACE`` lives in
00205| ``node.text`` rather than in a renderer flag -- the same lesson as the fork
00206| marker.  What rule 1 above says for appended *turns* therefore extends across
00207| the compaction boundary for this policy alone: because no earlier node's text
00208| changes, a turn's message list remains a byte-identical prefix of the next
00209| turn's even when a fold happens in between.
00210| """
00211| 
00212| from __future__ import annotations
00213| 
00214| from enum import Enum
00215| from typing import Any, Iterable, Mapping, Sequence
00216| 
00217| from .nodes import StateNode, canonical_bytes
00218| 
00219| # Kinds that NAIVE_MUTABLE has always rendered as append-only history.  The
00220| # append-only arms render every non-invariant node (see _body_nodes) so a
00221| # compaction summary/fork root is never dropped from the transcript.
00222| _HISTORY_KINDS = frozenset({"delta", "summary", "pointer"})
00223| 
00224| 
00225| class RenderPolicy(str, Enum):
00226|     POINTER = "pointer"
00227|     NAIVE_APPEND = "naive_append"
00228|     NAIVE_MUTABLE = "naive_mutable"
00229|     POINTER_FORK = "pointer_fork"
00230| 
00231| 
00232| def _volatile_block(volatile: Mapping[str, str]) -> str:
00233|     if not volatile:
00234|         return ""
00235|     return "\n".join(f"{key}={volatile[key]}" for key in sorted(volatile))
00236| 
00237| 
00238| def _history(chain: Sequence[StateNode]) -> list[StateNode]:
00239|     """Turn-bearing nodes (deltas/summaries), root invariant excluded."""
00240| 
00241|     return [n for n in chain if n.kind in _HISTORY_KINDS]
00242| 
00243| 
00244| def _body_nodes(chain: Sequence[StateNode]) -> list[StateNode]:
00245|     """Every node that carries conversation content: all but the invariant."""
00246| 
00247|     return [n for n in chain if n.kind != "invariant"]
00248| 
00249| 
00250| def _role(index: int) -> str:
00251|     return "user" if index % 2 == 0 else "assistant"
00252| 
00253| 
00254| def _invariant_content(
00255|     preamble: str,
00256|     salt: str,
00257|     chain: Sequence[StateNode],
00258|     *,
00259|     label_fork: bool,
00260| ) -> str:
00261|     from .salt import salted
00262| 
00263|     head = salted(salt, preamble)
00264|     if label_fork and chain and chain[0].kind == "fork":
00265|         head = f"{head}\n\n[chain] forked chain: root={chain[0].node_id}"
00266|     return head

00268| 
00269| def _bodies(chain: Sequence[StateNode]) -> list[dict[str, str]]:
00270|     return [
00271|         {"role": _role(i), "content": node.text}
00272|         for i, node in enumerate(_body_nodes(chain))
00273|     ]
00274| 
00275| 
00276| def _linear_messages(
00277|     chain: Sequence[StateNode],
00278|     *,
00279|     preamble: str,
00280|     salt: str,
00281|     label_fork: bool,
00282| ) -> list[dict[str, str]]:
00283|     """Salted invariant head, then every body verbatim and in order."""
00284| 
00285|     head = _invariant_content(preamble, salt, chain, label_fork=label_fork)
00286|     return [{"role": "system", "content": head}, *_bodies(chain)]
00287| 
00288| 
00289| def render(
00290|     policy: RenderPolicy | str,
00291|     chain: Iterable[StateNode],
00292|     *,
00293|     preamble: str,
00294|     volatile: Mapping[str, str],
00295|     salt: str,
00296| ) -> list[dict[str, str]]:
00297|     """Render a chain to OpenAI ``messages`` under ``policy``."""
00298| 
00299|     policy = RenderPolicy(policy)
00300|     nodes = list(chain)
00301|     if not nodes:
00302|         raise ValueError("cannot render an empty chain")
00303|     volatile = dict(volatile)
00304| 
00305|     if policy in (RenderPolicy.POINTER, RenderPolicy.NAIVE_APPEND):
00306|         return _linear_messages(nodes, preamble=preamble, salt=salt, label_fork=False)
00307| 
00308|     if policy is RenderPolicy.POINTER_FORK:
00309|         return _linear_messages(nodes, preamble=preamble, salt=salt, label_fork=True)
00310| 
00311|     if policy is RenderPolicy.NAIVE_MUTABLE:
00312|         from .salt import salted
00313| 
00314|         block = _volatile_block(volatile)
00315|         head = salted(salt, preamble)
00316|         if block:
00317|             head = f"{head}\n\n[volatile]\n{block}"
00318|         messages = [{"role": "system", "content": head}]
00319|         for i, node in enumerate(_history(nodes)):
00320|             messages.append({"role": _role(i), "content": node.text})
00321|         return messages
00322| 
00323|     raise AssertionError(f"unhandled policy {policy!r}")  # pragma: no cover
00324| 
00325| 
00326| def concatenated_content(messages: Sequence[Mapping[str, Any]]) -> str:
00327|     """Newline-joined contents of ``messages`` -- the information surface."""
00328| 
00329|     return "\n".join(str(message["content"]) for message in messages)
00330| 
00331| 
00332| def equal_information(
00333|     chain: Iterable[StateNode],
00334|     preamble: str,
00335|     salt: str,
00336| ) -> bool:
00337|     """Assert POINTER and NAIVE_APPEND carry the same information.
00338| 
00339|     The two renderings must have the same message count and the same
00340|     concatenated content for the same chain (a non-empty probe volatile is
00341|     passed, so an implementation that re-attaches volatile to one arm but not
00342|     the other is caught too).  Returns ``True`` on equality; raises
00343|     ``AssertionError`` naming both lengths otherwise.
00344|     """
00345| 
00346|     nodes = list(chain)
00347|     probe = {"step": "1", "focus": "probe"}
00348|     pointer = render(
00349|         RenderPolicy.POINTER, nodes, preamble=preamble, volatile=probe, salt=salt
00350|     )
00351|     naive = render(
00352|         RenderPolicy.NAIVE_APPEND, nodes, preamble=preamble, volatile=probe, salt=salt
00353|     )
00354|     pointer_text = concatenated_content(pointer)

00356|     if len(pointer) != len(naive) or pointer_text != naive_text:
00357|         raise AssertionError(
00358|             "POINTER and NAIVE_APPEND are not equal-information: "
00359|             f"{len(pointer)} vs {len(naive)} messages, "
00360|             f"{len(pointer_text)} vs {len(naive_text)} chars"
00361|         )
00362|     return True
00363| 
00364| 
00365| def render_bytes(
00366|     policy: RenderPolicy | str,
00367|     chain: Iterable[StateNode],
00368|     *,
00369|     preamble: str,
00370|     volatile: Mapping[str, str],
00371|     salt: str,
00372| ) -> bytes:
00373|     """Canonical JSON bytes of :func:`render`.

00375|     This is the serialised experiment payload, *not* a prefix surface on its
00376|     own: appending a message moves the array's closing ``]``, so a turn's
00377|     bytes are a prefix of the next turn's only up to its final byte.  Prefix

00379|     exact JSON relation is ``new.startswith(old[:-1] + b",")``.
00380|     """
00381| 
00382|     messages = render(
00383|         policy,
00384|         chain,
00385|         preamble=preamble,
00386|         volatile=volatile,
00387|         salt=salt,

00398| """Token-budget checks and compaction.
00399| 
00400| ``StateNode`` is immutable, so "editing" a chain always means constructing a
00401| new one.  That is what makes a fork distinguishable from an edit: compaction
00402| under ``FORK`` produces nodes with fresh content addresses whose ``parent_id``
00403| links point only at other *new* nodes -- never back into the chain being
00404| replaced.  The summariser is injected so the whole module is testable offline.
00405| 
00406| A fork is also distinguishable *inside the transcript*, not only in node
00407| metadata: every renderer emits ``node.text`` and none emits ``node.kind``, so
00408| a fork node whose text was just the summary would render byte-for-byte like an
00409| in-place summary (U13's finding -- U4/U5 compared two arms that were literally
00410| the same prompt).  The fork node's text therefore begins with a
00411| content-addressed provenance marker naming the folded head's last node id and
00412| the chain hash being forked from; ``SUMMARISE_IN_PLACE`` rewrites the head
00413| silently and carries no such pointer.
00414| 
00415| ``APPEND_NOTE`` is the fourth policy and the only one that never rewrites the
00416| head.  ``SLIDING_WINDOW``, ``SUMMARISE_IN_PLACE`` and ``FORK`` all construct a
00417| new chain out of the retained tail, so the folded head -- and, for the first
00418| two, the invariant preamble with it -- simply stops being part of the prompt;
00419| the first message after the header therefore changes at every compaction
00420| point.  ``APPEND_NOTE`` instead carries every existing node through untouched,
00421| as the *same object* (same text, same ``node_id``, same parent link), and adds
00422| one summary node at the tail whose text begins with a marker naming the last
00423| folded node and the pre-compaction chain hash.  Nothing is edited and nothing
00424| is removed, so the pre-note prefix of the chain -- and of every renderer's
00425| message list -- stays byte-identical across the compaction.  That is the
00426| property no other policy has, and it is what makes cache reuse across a
00427| compaction point measurable; the price is that the prompt grows instead of
00428| shrinking, because this policy *annotates* the fold rather than enforcing the
00429| budget.
00430| """
00431| 
00432| from __future__ import annotations
00433| 
00434| from enum import Enum
00435| from typing import Any, Callable, Iterable, Sequence
00436| 
00437| from .nodes import StateNode
00438| 
00439| Summarizer = Callable[[str], str]
00440| 
00441| 
00442| class CompactionPolicy(str, Enum):
00443|     SUMMARISE_IN_PLACE = "summarise_in_place"
00444|     SLIDING_WINDOW = "sliding_window"
00445|     FORK = "fork"
00446|     APPEND_NOTE = "append_note"
00447| 
00448| 
00449| def default_est_tokens(text: str) -> int:
00450|     """Cheap offline token estimate: ~4 characters per token, minimum 1."""
00451| 
00452|     return max(1, (len(text) + 3) // 4)
00453| 
00454| 
00455| def _total(chain: Sequence[StateNode], est_tokens: Callable[[str], int]) -> int:
00456|     return sum(est_tokens(node.text) for node in chain)
00457| 
00458| 
00459| def needs_compaction(
00460|     chain: Iterable[StateNode],
00461|     *,
00462|     budget_tokens: int,
00463|     est_tokens: Callable[[str], int],
00464| ) -> bool:
00465|     """True when the chain's estimated token count exceeds ``budget_tokens``."""
00466| 
00467|     if budget_tokens < 0:
00468|         raise ValueError("budget_tokens must be >= 0")
00469|     return _total(list(chain), est_tokens) > budget_tokens
00470| 
00471| 
00472| def _rebuild(
00473|     texts: Sequence[tuple[str, str, dict[str, Any]]],
00474| ) -> list[StateNode]:
00475|     """Create ``(text, kind, meta)`` nodes in order, linking each to the prior."""
00476| 
00477|     out: list[StateNode] = []
00478|     parent: StateNode | None = None
00479|     for text, kind, meta in texts:
00480|         node = StateNode.create(text, kind, parent=parent, **meta)
00481|         out.append(node)
00482|         parent = node
00483|     return out
00484| 
00485| 
00486| def compact(
00487|     chain: Iterable[StateNode],
00488|     policy: CompactionPolicy | str,
00489|     *,
00490|     keep_last: int,
00491|     summarizer: Summarizer,
00492|     est_tokens: Callable[[str], int] = default_est_tokens,
00493| ) -> tuple[list[StateNode], dict[str, Any]]:
00494|     """Compact ``chain`` and return ``(new_chain, event)``.
00495| 
00496|     ``summarizer`` is called at most once, on the concatenated text of the
00497|     nodes that are folded/dropped, so a stub suffices in tests.
00498|     """
00499| 
00500|     policy = CompactionPolicy(policy)
00501|     chain = list(chain)
00502|     if not chain:
00503|         raise ValueError("cannot compact an empty chain")
00504|     if keep_last < 0:
00505|         raise ValueError("keep_last must be >= 0")
00506| 
00507|     tokens_before = _total(chain, est_tokens)
00508|     cut = max(0, len(chain) - keep_last)
00509|     head, tail = chain[:cut], chain[cut:]
00510|     summary_text = summarizer("\n\n".join(node.text for node in head)) if head else ""
00511| 
00512|     if policy is CompactionPolicy.SLIDING_WINDOW:
00513|         new_chain = _rebuild([(node.text, "delta", {"dropped": cut}) for node in tail])
00514|         edited = [node.node_id for node in head]
00515|         forked = False
00516|     elif policy is CompactionPolicy.SUMMARISE_IN_PLACE:
00517|         specs: list[tuple[str, str, dict[str, Any]]] = [
00518|             (summary_text, "summary", {"compacted": True, "kept": len(tail)})
00519|         ]
00520|         specs += [
00521|             (node.text, "delta" if node.kind == "summary" else node.kind, {"kept": True})
00522|             for node in tail
00523|         ]
00524|         new_chain = _rebuild(specs)
00525|         edited = [node.node_id for node in head]
00526|         forked = False
00527|     elif policy is CompactionPolicy.FORK:
00528|         # The marker is the fork's identity, so it must be content-addressed:
00529|         # the replaced head's last node id pins the prefix that is folded away,
00530|         # and the pre-compaction chain hash pins the chain being forked from.
00531|         # Both are already hashes, so the fork node's own address commits to
00532|         # exactly what it replaced.  ``SUMMARISE_IN_PLACE`` emits no marker --
00533|         # which is why the two policies used to render identical prompts.
00534|         replaced_head_id = head[-1].node_id if head else "none"
00535|         fork_tag = {"forked": True, "forked_from": chain[-1].chain_hash}
00536|         marker = (
00537|             f"[fork] replaces head through {replaced_head_id}; "
00538|             f"forked_from {chain[-1].chain_hash}"
00539|         )
